title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'Analysis situs', an attempt at a combinatorial or 'tame' topology. The basic object is a 'structure d'inégalités' M: a set of 'elements' (think closed tame subsets) with several relations:
- X ≤ Y, inclusion;
- X ≪ Y and X ≪° Y, inclusion in the interior;
- X |·| Y, disjointness;
- X ∥ Y, apparently 'meeting' or 'having a common minorant';
- X ≭ Y, compatibility: X and Y lie in a common figure.

A figure F ∈ Fig(M) is a family (X_i), i ∈ I, of elements indexed by a poset I, behaving like the closed strata of a stratification. Distinct members are pairwise |·|-related in the appropriate sense. F̃ (respectively X̃) is the associated poset of elements generated by F (respectively the elements under X). The previous page proposed morphisms of inequality structures φ: M → M' preserving a) ≤, b) ≪ and ≪°, and c) |·|.

This page.
1. Grothendieck adds condition d): for every X ∈ M, φ induces a bijection X̃ ≅ X̃' where X' = φ(X). This is a local-isomorphism or 'étale' condition on down-sets.
2. Cor. 1: a), c), d) imply that φ maps figures to figures, and that φ|F is injective (indeed an isomorphism of the index posets I = F̃ → I'). By the previous proposition it suffices to check injectivity on F. For X ≠ Y in F one has X |·| Y, hence φ(X) |·| φ(Y), hence φ(X) ≠ φ(Y).
3. Cor. 2: φ preserves compatibility (X ≭ Y ⇒ X' ≭ Y') and ∥. Compatibility means lying in a common figure, so Cor. 1 applies.
4. Cor. 3: for X, Y ∈ F̃, φ reflects as well as preserves ≤ and ∥ (X ≤ Y ⇔ X' ≤ Y', X ∥ Y ⇔ X' ∥ Y'). The first follows from Cor. 1. The second uses the fact that ∥ is read off the ordered set I = F̃ (existence of a common minorant), which is transported isomorphically onto I' = φ(I).

Margin, dated 17.7.86, i.e. after the folder's date range: condition d) 'should be weakened'. The next page likewise worries that the hypothesis is very strong; for continuous maps it seems to force something like open surjective maps.

Purpose: to set up the category of inequality structures so that morphisms induce maps of figures compatible with union and intersection of compatible figures (Cors. 4–6 on the next page).
errors: The injectivity argument in Cor. 1 needs |·| to be irreflexive on the elements involved (no 'empty' element X with X |·| X). This is implicit and not stated on the page.

Condition d) is very strong. Grothendieck himself flags this (margin of 17.7.86, and next page) and suspects it excludes natural examples such as non-open maps. The corollaries thus rest on a provisional hypothesis.
Cor. 3's justification of the ∥ equivalence is only sketched and partly illegible; it depends on characterizing ∥ intrinsically inside F̃.

ideas.what: Morphisms of an axiomatic 'inequality structure' (tame-topology lattice of closed sets with relations ≤, ≪, |·|) required to induce bijections on the down-set of each element
ideas.modern_name: Local isomorphism / discrete fibration of posets (étale map for the Alexandrov topology); morphisms of stratified spaces inducing isomorphisms on link/face posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discrete fibrations: Grothendieck (SGA1, fibered categories); étale maps of posets/face posets: folklore
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Morphisms preserving figures (stratification-like families) and inducing order isomorphisms on their index posets; preservation of compatibility and of the meeting relation
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of stratified sets / face posets (o-minimal or semi-algebraic stratification theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather), o-minimal geometry (van den Dries)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly leaves open the right weakening of the local-isomorphism condition d) for morphisms of his axiomatic 'inequality structures'. This is part of the never-completed axiomatization of tame topology announced in the Esquisse.
missed.quote: Il semble qu'on ait besoin aussi de la condition d) ∀ X∈M, φ induit une bijection X̃ → X̃' ... [marge 17.7.86] Cette condition d) devrait ... être affaiblie
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild interest for anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's tame-topology programme. The mathematics itself (étale/discrete-fibration-type conditions on posets of strata) is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are foundational, routine corollaries in an unpublished axiomatic set-up. The only notable points are the 'étale on down-sets' condition and Grothendieck's own dated doubt about it, of historical rather than mathematical novelty.
transcription_corrections: Cor. 2 reads 'X ≭ Y ⟹ X' ≭ Y'' (compatibility symbol, as in 'F ≭ G' on the next page), not 'X ≰ Y'. Likewise 'X ≭ Y signifie que X,Y font partie d'une figure F'.
Insertion in Cor. 1 is roughly: 'et φ|F est injective (et induit un iso. d'ensembles ordonnés) (... pour I = F̃)'.
Margin date is 17.7.86, a later addition beyond the folder's range 26/06–04/07. The margin reads roughly: 'Cette condition d) devrait [peut-être] être affaiblie ... !'.
The final lines concern ∥ being characterized in the ordered set I = F̃ (existence of a common minorant), transported to I' = φ(I).
